title: Creating & Configuring Repositories
summary: Master public vs private repositories, branch protection rules, templates, and collaborator access.
steps: Navigate to github.com and click 'New' repository.
Choose a repository name using kebab-case (e.g., project-backend).
Set visibility: Public (visible to world) or Private (only you and invited collaborators).
Configure Branch Protection Rules in Settings > Branches to require code reviews before merging into main.
proTip: Never commit credentials or database passwords. Add .env to .gitignore before your first commit.

title: Pull Requests & Code Reviews
summary: How professional engineering teams propose, review, test, and merge code changes safely.
steps: Push your feature branch to GitHub: git push -u origin feature-name
Click 'Compare & pull request' on the GitHub repository homepage.
Add a descriptive title and structured summary (What changed, Why, How to test).
Request review from peers. Reviewers can approve, request changes, or leave inline comments.
Once approved and CI checks pass, click 'Squash and merge' or 'Merge pull request'.
proTip: Keep PRs small (under 400 lines). Small PRs get reviewed 2x faster and have fewer bugs.

title: Forking & Open Source Contribution
summary: Contribute to third-party repositories without having direct write access to the upstream repo.
steps: Click the 'Fork' button on the top right of the target GitHub repository.
Clone your personal fork: git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/repo.git
Add the original repo as an upstream remote: git remote add upstream https://github.com/ORIGINAL-OWNER/repo.git
Fetch upstream changes regularly: git fetch upstream && git merge upstream/main
Push changes to your fork and submit a Pull Request back to the original repository.
proTip: Always create a new branch for each contribution rather than committing directly on main.

title: SSH Keys & Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
summary: Connect securely to GitHub from your terminal without entering passwords on every push.
steps: Generate an Ed25519 SSH key: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
Start the ssh-agent: eval "$(ssh-agent -s)" and add key: ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
Copy your public key: cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
Go to GitHub Settings > SSH and GPG keys > 'New SSH key', paste and save.
Verify with: ssh -T git@github.com
proTip: GitHub no longer accepts account passwords for terminal operations. SSH keys or Personal Access Tokens (PAT) are mandatory.

title: Hosting Free Websites with GitHub Pages
summary: Host client-side static web apps, documentation, portfolios, and project demos directly from a repository.
steps: Ensure your repository contains an index.html file in the root or /docs directory.
Navigate to repository Settings > Pages.
Under 'Build and deployment', choose Source: 'Deploy from a branch'.
Select branch: 'main' and folder: '/ (root)' or '/docs', then click Save.
Your site will be live in 1-2 minutes at https://<username>.github.io/<repo-name>/
proTip: GitHub Pages only supports static HTML, CSS, and clientside JS. Backend servers (Node.js/Python) require platforms like Render, Vercel, or Railway.

title: GitHub Actions & CI/CD Pipelines
summary: Automate unit testing, linting, build verification, and deployment on every push and pull request.
steps: Create a directory in your repo: .github/workflows/
Create a workflow YAML file, e.g., ci.yml.
Define triggers (on: [push, pull_request]), runner OS (runs-on: ubuntu-latest), and test steps.
Commit and push. GitHub will automatically run the workflow and report status checks on your PR.
proTip: Public repositories get unlimited free GitHub Actions minutes for standard runners.
